symptom: PC in VLAN 30 cannot reach PCs in VLAN 10 even though inter-VLAN routing is configured on router-on-a-stick
topology_note: Router R1 has subinterfaces Gi0/0.10 and Gi0/0.30; SW1 trunk to R1
show_command_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 10 active Fa0/1-5; VLAN 20 active Fa0/6-10; VLAN 30 not found in table. show interfaces trunk: Gi0/1 trunking VLANs allowed 1-29. show ip interface brief: Gi0/0.10 up/up 192.168.10.1; Gi0/0.30 up/up 192.168.30.1
expected_fault: VLAN 30 missing from VLAN database; trunk not allowing VLAN 30

symptom: All PCs in VLAN 20 get IP 169.254.x.x addresses
topology_note: SW2 has DHCP server configured on VLAN 20 SVI
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: Pool VLAN20 network 192.168.20.0/24 default-router 192.168.20.1 dns-server 8.8.8.8. show ip dhcp binding: No bindings. show interfaces vlan 20: Vlan20 is up line protocol is down
expected_fault: DHCP pool exists but VLAN 20 SVI is down so DISCOVER never reaches server

symptom: PC0 can ping its default gateway but cannot reach 8.8.8.8 or any external IP
topology_note: Small office topology with ISP router; NAT overload configured on border router
show_command_outputs: show ip nat translations: Pro Inside global Inside local Outside local Outside global — empty table. show running-config interface Gi0/1: ip nat inside missing. show access-lists 10: permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255
expected_fault: NAT inside not applied to LAN interface Gi0/1

symptom: Users can ping by IP but not by hostname; nslookup returns timeout
topology_note: SOHO network; DNS server 192.168.1.253 configured in DHCP pool
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: dns-server 192.168.1.253. ping 192.168.1.253: Success rate 0%. show ip arp: 192.168.1.253 incomplete
expected_fault: DNS server IP unreachable; host is down or misconfigured

symptom: PC in 10.0.0.0/24 cannot reach server in 172.16.0.0/24; router has two interfaces
topology_note: R1 is directly connected to both subnets
show_command_outputs: show ip route: 10.0.0.0/24 C directly connected Gi0/0; 172.16.0.0/24 C directly connected Gi0/1. show ip interface brief: Gi0/0 10.0.0.1 up/down; Gi0/1 172.16.0.1 up/up. show interfaces Gi0/0: Gi0/0 is up line protocol is down — cable unplugged
expected_fault: Gi0/0 line protocol down due to Layer 1 issue; no route usable

symptom: SSH from management PC to SW3 is refused; Telnet works fine
topology_note: SW3 has both Telnet and SSH configured
show_command_outputs: show line vty 0 4: transport input telnet. show ip ssh: SSH enabled version 2.0. show running-config: line vty 0 4 transport input telnet
expected_fault: VTY lines not configured to accept SSH; transport input telnet only

symptom: Wireless clients associate to AP but get no IP address
topology_note: AP connected to SW1 Fa0/24 in access mode VLAN 1; DHCP on R1
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: Pool WIRELESS network 192.168.50.0/24. show interfaces Fa0/24 switchport: Access Mode VLAN 1. show vlan brief: VLAN 50 active Fa0/20-23
expected_fault: AP port in VLAN 1 but DHCP pool is for VLAN 50; client DISCOVERs wrong VLAN

symptom: Guest SSID clients can reach each other and corporate servers; isolation not working
topology_note: Dual-SSID AP; corporate SSID on VLAN 10; guest SSID on VLAN 20
show_command_outputs: show running-config: dot11 ssid GUEST vlan 20 guest-mode. show vlan brief: VLAN 20 active Fa0/15. show ip route: 192.168.10.0/24 C Gi0/0.10; 192.168.20.0/24 C Gi0/0.20. show access-lists: empty
expected_fault: No ACL preventing guest VLAN 20 from reaching VLAN 10; inter-VLAN routing allows full access

symptom: PC1 (192.168.1.10) cannot ping PC2 (192.168.1.20); both in same VLAN 1
topology_note: Both PCs on SW1; no router involved
show_command_outputs: show ip interface brief: VLAN1 192.168.1.254 up/up. show mac address-table: 0001.0001.0001 Fa0/1; 0002.0002.0002 Fa0/3. show interfaces Fa0/2: Fa0/2 is administratively down
expected_fault: PC2 connected to Fa0/2 which is shut down; Layer 2 connectivity broken

symptom: All 30 PCs on floor 2 suddenly lose connectivity after switch config change
topology_note: Access layer SW2 reconfigured by junior admin
show_command_outputs: show vlan brief: VLAN 1 active Fa0/1-24. show interfaces trunk: no trunk interfaces found. show running-config SW2: switchport mode access on all uplink ports
expected_fault: Uplink port to distribution switch changed from trunk to access; all inter-VLAN traffic blocked

symptom: PC cannot obtain IP via DHCP; DHCP server is on a different subnet
topology_note: DHCP relay (ip helper-address) scenario
show_command_outputs: show ip interface brief: Gi0/0 192.168.1.1 up/up. show running-config Gi0/0: no ip helper-address configured. show ip dhcp binding: empty. ping 10.10.10.10: Success rate 100%
expected_fault: ip helper-address not configured on router interface facing client subnet

symptom: PC gets correct IP from DHCP but cannot reach default gateway 192.168.1.1
topology_note: DHCP pool has wrong default-router configured
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: default-router 192.168.1.254. show ip interface brief: Gi0/0 192.168.1.1 up/up. ipconfig: Default Gateway 192.168.1.254. ping 192.168.1.254: Request timeout
expected_fault: DHCP pool advertises .254 as gateway but router SVI is .1; no host at .254

symptom: PC0 can reach 192.168.2.0/24 but not 10.0.0.0/8; static route exists
topology_note: R1 has static route to 10.0.0.0/8 but next-hop is wrong
show_command_outputs: show ip route: S 10.0.0.0/8 [1/0] via 192.168.99.2. show ip arp: 192.168.99.2 incomplete. show interfaces Serial0/0/0: Serial0/0/0 is up line protocol is up 192.168.99.1/30
expected_fault: Next-hop 192.168.99.2 not reachable (ARP incomplete on serial link; should use exit interface)

symptom: Web server in DMZ is unreachable from internet; NAT static entry exists
topology_note: PAT plus static NAT for web server 192.168.10.100
show_command_outputs: show ip nat translations: tcp 203.0.113.1:80 --- 192.168.10.100:80. show access-lists 101: deny tcp any host 192.168.10.100 eq 80. show interfaces Gi0/0: ip access-group 101 in
expected_fault: ACL 101 denies TCP port 80 inbound before NAT translation is applied

symptom: R2 does not see routes to 172.16.0.0/16 via OSPF; adjacency is up
topology_note: OSPF area 0; R1 and R2 directly connected
show_command_outputs: show ip ospf neighbor: 10.0.0.1 FULL/DR. show ip route: no OSPF routes. show ip ospf interface Gi0/1: network type BROADCAST hello 10 dead 40. show running-config R1: network 172.16.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 1
expected_fault: 172.16.0.0/16 advertised into area 1 on R1 but inter-area route not propagating because ABR missing

symptom: EIGRP neighborship flaps every 15 seconds between R1 and R2
topology_note: EIGRP AS 100
show_command_outputs: show ip eigrp neighbors: 10.1.1.2 H 0 Uptime 00:00:12. show running-config R1: ip hello-interval eigrp 100 5; ip hold-time eigrp 100 10. show running-config R2: ip hello-interval eigrp 100 15; ip hold-time eigrp 100 15
expected_fault: R2 hold-time (15s) barely exceeds R1 hello (5s) but R1 hold-time (10s) less than R2 hello (15s); neighborship resets

symptom: PC in 192.168.10.0/24 gets IP correctly but cannot ping 192.168.10.1 gateway
topology_note: Default gateway 192.168.10.1 is a router subinterface
show_command_outputs: show ip interface brief: Gi0/0.10 192.168.10.1 up/up. show interfaces Gi0/0: Gi0/0 is administratively down. show interfaces Gi0/0.10: Gi0/0.10 is up line protocol is down
expected_fault: Parent interface Gi0/0 is shut; subinterfaces inherit down state even though shown as up/down

symptom: Clients behind NAT get response from google.com but not from 192.168.100.0/24 internal server
topology_note: Hairpin NAT / NAT loopback needed for internal server accessed by FQDN
show_command_outputs: show ip nat translations: tcp 203.0.113.5:80 --- 192.168.100.5:80 only from outside. show running-config: no ip nat inside source static — loopback not configured. ping 192.168.100.5 from R1: success
expected_fault: NAT loopback not configured; inside clients trying to reach server via public IP get dropped

symptom: Extended ACL blocks all traffic from 192.168.5.0/24 to 10.0.0.0/8 but also blocks ICMP returns
topology_note: ACL applied outbound on wrong interface
show_command_outputs: show access-lists 110: 10 permit tcp 192.168.5.0 0.0.0.255 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 established; 20 deny ip 192.168.5.0 0.0.0.255 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255; 30 permit ip any any. show ip interface: Gi0/1 outbound ACL 110
expected_fault: ACL sequence wrong; established check on line 10 means new sessions hit deny on line 20; should flip order

symptom: New PC added to VLAN 40 cannot communicate; all other VLANs working
topology_note: VLAN 40 created on SW1 but not on SW2
show_command_outputs: show vlan brief SW1: VLAN 40 active Fa0/20. show vlan brief SW2: VLAN 40 not found. show interfaces trunk: SW1 Gi0/1 trunking allowed VLANs 1-39
expected_fault: VLAN 40 not in trunk allowed list between SW1 and SW2; also missing on SW2

symptom: DHCP clients on VLAN 10 get addresses from wrong pool intended for VLAN 20
topology_note: Two DHCP pools on same router; VLANs share physical interface
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool VLAN10: network 192.168.10.0/24 default-router 192.168.10.1. show ip dhcp pool VLAN20: network 192.168.20.0/24 default-router 192.168.20.1. show ip interface brief: no VLAN 10 SVI; Gi0/0.20 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: VLAN 10 SVI missing; DHCP discovers land on wrong subinterface matching VLAN 20 pool

symptom: Router cannot find DNS entry for internal domain corp.local; external DNS works
topology_note: Split-DNS setup; internal DNS 192.168.1.10
show_command_outputs: show ip name-server: 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4. show hosts: no static entries. ping 192.168.1.10: success. nslookup corp.local 192.168.1.10: answer 192.168.1.50
expected_fault: Router ip name-server only lists public DNS; internal DNS 192.168.1.10 not configured

symptom: Wireless client connects to SSID but cannot reach internet; wired clients fine
topology_note: AP in autonomous mode; WPA2-PSK SSID HOME
show_command_outputs: show dot11 associations: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff associated. show interfaces Dot11Radio0: Dot11Radio0 is up line protocol is up. show ip route: 0.0.0.0/0 not found. show ip interface brief: BVI1 192.168.1.254 up/up; no default route
expected_fault: AP missing default route; BVI1 has LAN IP but no gateway or default route configured

symptom: WPA2-Enterprise clients prompted for certificate but AP not rejecting wrong password users
topology_note: RADIUS server integration issue
show_command_outputs: show running-config: dot11 ssid CORP authentication open eap RADIUS_GROUP. show radius server-group RADIUS_GROUP: server 192.168.1.20. ping 192.168.1.20: success rate 0%
expected_fault: RADIUS server unreachable (ping fails); AP falls back to open auth allowing anyone

symptom: PC1 10.10.10.10/24 cannot ping PC2 10.10.10.20/24 on same switch; both show connected
topology_note: Two PCs on SW1 in VLAN 1; SW1 is layer 2 only
show_command_outputs: show mac address-table: 0001.0001.0001 Fa0/1; 0002.0002.0002 Fa0/2. show interfaces Fa0/1: Fa0/1 is up/up. show interfaces Fa0/2: Fa0/2 is up/up. show vlan brief: VLAN 1 active Fa0/1 Fa0/2. ipconfig PC1: 10.10.10.10/24 gw 10.10.10.1. ipconfig PC2: 10.10.10.20/255.255.0.0
expected_fault: Subnet mask mismatch; PC1 /24 sees PC2 /16 — PC2 responds from different broadcast domain

symptom: All PCs get 169.254.x.x; DHCP server is on R1 Gi0/0 192.168.1.1/24
topology_note: 10 PCs on SW1 connected to R1
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 default-router 192.168.1.1. show ip dhcp excluded-address: 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.200. show ip dhcp binding: empty. show ip interface brief Gi0/0: up/up
expected_fault: Excluded range covers .1 to .200; pool only has .201-.254 — pool exhaustion unlikely with 10 PCs; check excluded range is accidentally too wide leaving no allocatable addresses (.201-.254 = 54 addresses — actually valid). Recheck: excluded 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.254 — full range excluded leaving zero allocatable addresses

symptom: NAT translations table shows entries but ISP router drops returning packets
topology_note: PAT configured; ISP router has route back to 10.0.0.0/8
show_command_outputs: show ip nat translations: udp 203.0.113.10:1024 --- 10.0.0.5:1024. show ip route on ISP: 10.0.0.0/8 via 203.0.113.1. show interfaces Gi0/0 on border router: ip address 203.0.113.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: ISP has route back to 10.0.0.0/8 sourced from border router; returning packets hit NAT but inside global 203.0.113.10 not owned by this router — wrong outside global IP in NAT

symptom: After adding ACL to filter Telnet traffic permit-any at end of ACL was removed
topology_note: SW1 management ACL modified
show_command_outputs: show access-lists 10: 10 deny tcp any any eq 23. show ip interface vlan1: inbound ACL 10. show interfaces vlan1: up/up
expected_fault: ACL 10 has only deny statement; implicit deny-all blocks everything including ICMP and DHCP — permit any any missing

symptom: R1 has two paths to 192.168.50.0/24 via OSPF; traffic always takes the slower serial link
topology_note: OSPF cost not manually set; both paths in routing table
show_command_outputs: show ip route: O 192.168.50.0/24 [110/65] via 10.0.0.2 Serial0/0; O 192.168.50.0/24 [110/2] via 10.1.1.2 Gi0/1. show ip ospf interface Serial0/0: cost 64. show ip ospf interface Gi0/1: cost 1
expected_fault: OSPF load-balances over both paths; but if traffic always uses serial the routing table shows equal cost — actually costs are 65 vs 2; lower metric via Gi0/1 should win. Likely CEF / per-flow hashing sending one flow to serial

symptom: PC in 192.168.1.0/24 can reach internet but cannot reach 192.168.2.0/24 server
topology_note: Two LANs on R1; both directly connected
show_command_outputs: show ip route: C 192.168.1.0/24 Gi0/0; C 192.168.2.0/24 Gi0/1. show ip interface brief: Gi0/0 up/up; Gi0/1 up/up. show access-lists 100: 10 permit ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 8.8.8.8; 20 deny ip 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.2.0 0.0.0.255; 30 permit ip any any. show ip interface Gi0/0: outbound ACL 100
expected_fault: ACL 100 explicitly denies 192.168.1.0 to 192.168.2.0 on Gi0/0 outbound

symptom: SW1 VLAN 10 SVI is up but hosts cannot reach router in VLAN 20
topology_note: Layer 3 switch doing inter-VLAN routing; ip routing enabled
show_command_outputs: show ip interface brief: Vlan10 192.168.10.1 up/up; Vlan20 192.168.20.1 up/up. show vlan brief: VLAN 10 Fa0/1-5; VLAN 20 Fa0/6-10. show ip route: C 192.168.10.0/24; C 192.168.20.0/24. ipconfig on VLAN10 host: default gateway 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: Host default gateway wrong; VLAN 10 host configured with VLAN 20 SVI IP as gateway

symptom: DNS queries succeed from router but fail from client PC; same DNS server configured
topology_note: SOHO; DNS 8.8.8.8 in DHCP and static on router
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool: dns-server 8.8.8.8. ipconfig PC: DNS 8.8.8.8. ping 8.8.8.8 from PC: success. show access-lists 150: deny udp any any eq 53. show ip interface Gi0/0: inbound ACL 150
expected_fault: ACL 150 blocking UDP port 53 inbound on LAN interface; DNS queries from PCs dropped

symptom: WPA2-PSK clients connect to SSID CORP but session drops every 2 minutes
topology_note: Autonomous AP; TKIP encryption selected
show_command_outputs: show running-config: encryption mode ciphers tkip. show dot11 associations: Auth-Alg Open; Cipher-type TKIP. show interfaces Dot11Radio0: dot11 ssid CORP authentication shared
expected_fault: TKIP known vulnerable and incompatible with some clients; 802.11n drops to 54Mbps; shared key auth with TKIP causes periodic re-keying failures

symptom: Two routers R1 and R2 both claim IP 10.0.0.1; duplicate IP detected
topology_note: R1 and R2 on same segment; both configured /30 same address
show_command_outputs: show ip interface brief R1: Gi0/0 10.0.0.1/30. show ip interface brief R2: Gi0/0 10.0.0.1/30. show ip arp R1: Internet 10.0.0.1 0011.2233.4455. show ip arp R2: Internet 10.0.0.1 aabb.ccdd.eeff — conflict
expected_fault: Duplicate IP 10.0.0.1 on same segment; ARP conflict causes intermittent drops

symptom: DHCP clients get address in wrong subnet 10.99.0.0/24 instead of 10.1.0.0/24
topology_note: Three DHCP pools on R1; relay configured
show_command_outputs: show ip dhcp pool VLAN1: network 10.1.0.0/24 default-router 10.1.0.1. show ip dhcp pool TEST: network 10.99.0.0/24 default-router 10.99.0.1. show running-config: ip helper-address 10.1.0.100 on wrong interface; helper on Gi0/0 pointing to DHCP server at 10.1.0.100 but DHCP server at 10.1.0.100 has TEST pool as default pool
expected_fault: DHCP server returns address from TEST pool because it is the first matching pool for the relayed DISCOVER
